Summary Brookfield Infrastructure Partners L.P. has dipped from its 52-week high as surging Treasury yields push its dividend yield to a negative spread over the U.S. 10-year Treasury rate. The firm saw year-over-year FFO per unit growth of 10% in the second quarter and is trading at a 10.5x multiple to this metric annualized. I rate BIP as a Hold, reflecting continued volatility with U.S. Treasuries and ongoing inflationary geopolitical uncertainty.
